summary: Katsumi Okimoto specializes in Buddhist studies. He was a graduate student at the University of Tokyo from circa 1971 to 1973 and served as director at Hanazono University from circa 1980 to 2014.

Katsumi Tanabe is a scholar in history and archaeology, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and Indology. He studied at the University of Tokyo (~1961–1971) and held positions at Kanazawa University (~1993–2004) and Chuo University (~2004–2011).

Katsutoshi Ono worked in history and archaeology, Buddhist studies, and Sinology. After studying at Kyoto University (~1928–1931), he held posts at Kansai University and Ryukoku University (~1963–1976).
Kavita Singh was a scholar in history, archaeology, and Indology. She completed her studies at Lady Shri Ram College for Women (~1982–1985) and Panjab University (~1987–1996).

Kazi Dawa Samdup worked in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He was headmaster at Maharaja's Bhutia Boarding School in 1919 and taught at the University of Calcutta (~1919–1922), teaching Walter Yeeling Evans-Wentz and Herbert Bruce Hannah.
Kazu Uehara specialized in history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies. He studied at Kyushu University (~1946–1949) and held an academic post at Seijo University (~1972–1995).
Kazuaki Komine works in Japanology and Buddhist studies. He held academic posts at Tokushima University (~1979–1990) and Rikkyo University (~1994–2013), where he became Professor Emeritus.
Kazufumi Oki is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology who studied at Kyoto University (~1972–1977). He served as an assistant professor at Shuchiin University and taught Shinshu Kusumoto.

Kazuharu Mizuno studied at Nagoya University (~1978–1982), Hokkaido University (~1982–1984), and Tokyo Metropolitan University (~1984–1989). From circa 2004 to 2024, he was Professor of Department of Geography at Kyoto University's Graduate School of Letters.

Kazuhiko Yoshida studied linguistics and Indology at Sophia University, Kyoto University, and Cornell University under Jay Jasanoff. He held academic posts at Nagoya City University (~1986–1993) and as a professor at Kyoto University (~2002–2020).
Kazuhiro Furuta is an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar who served as Dean at Otani University and worked as an editor and publisher at the Otani Society in 1991.
Kazuhiro Kawasaki is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He completed doctoral studies at Koyasan University around 2005 and worked there as a researcher.
Kazuhiro Yamamoto works in Indology and philosophy. He studied at Silpakorn University from circa 2004 to 2009 under doctoral supervisors Samniang Leurmsai and Chirapat Prapandvidya.

Kazunobu Matsuda studied under Shiro Matsumoto and at Otani University (~1974–1979). A Buddhist studies and Indology scholar, he held posts at Otani University, Kyoto University, the Eastern Institute, and Bukkyo University (Professor in 2009).

Kazuo Hyodo studied at Kyoto and Otani universities under scholars including Hajime Sakurabe and Nobuchiyo Kotani. Working in Buddhist studies and Indology, he served at Otani University (2000–2005) and the Otani Society.

Kazuo Kano works in Buddhist studies, Indology, and Tibetology, having studied at Kyoto University and the University of Hamburg. He held posts at the University of Hamburg, Kyoto University, Koyasan University (~2007–2017), and Komazawa University (~2017).

Kazuo Matsumura is a religious studies scholar who studied at Hitotsubashi University (~1972–1976). He taught Mizuho Okita and held academic appointments at Tenri University (~1989–1995) and Wako University (~2002–2019).
Kazuo Okabe studied Buddhist studies and Sinology at Komazawa University (~1954–1958). He later served as a professor at Komazawa University (~1984–2006) and taught Jamie Hubbard.

Kazuo Osumi was a scholar of history, archaeology, Japanology, and Buddhist studies. After studying at the University of Tokyo (~1951–1955), he held posts at Hokkaido University (~1968–1976) and Tokyo Woman's Christian University (~1976–2003).
Kazuo Oyamada works in Buddhist studies, history and archaeology, and Japanology. He studied at Tamagawa University (~1971–1975) and held a post at Rissho University around 1989.
